guide.summary: A light-powered cell that builds a glassy shell and needs silicate to grow.
guide.biology: Some real algae build delicate glass-like shells from silica dissolved in the water around them.
guide.rules: Lives in water only and does not swim. Turns carbon dioxide into half body and half sugar, releasing oxygen, in proportion to local light. Needs mineral nutrients, and binds 0.10 silicate into its shell for every unit of new body, so it grows slower when silicate runs short. Starts with shell mineral equal to 0.10 of its starting body, and splits it when it divides. When it dies or is eaten, all its shell mineral falls as grit, which dissolves back into silicate at 1% per second. The shell gives no protection. Prey for Amoeba, Rotifer, Waterbear and Wheelgrazer.
guide.example: Grow Glasswheels with and without a silicate patch and compare how fast each group grows.
